turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (PATIENT): Oh hi, sorry, your parking lot is a maze, I looped it twice. Um, it's my cheek and this tooth. Throbbing, and the side of my face is all swollen.
[SEG0002] person_2 (CAREGIVER): She almost didn't come. Kept waiting on the dentist to call.
[SEG0003] person_1 (PATIENT): They're not calling. Office is closed for a conference, the voicemail just cuts off, nobody picks up. They did a crown and then this started.
[SEG0004] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay. So the crown, then the pain. Which tooth, and how long's it been throbbing?
[SEG0005] person_1 (PATIENT): Lower right, way in the back. Crown was Friday? No, Thursday. Thursday. Throbbing for three days, like a drum in the tooth.
[SEG0006] person_1 (PATIENT): My neighbor got a crown and ate steak the next day, so I thought this would just quit, but...
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mm. Cheek swollen those same three days?
[SEG0008] person_1 (PATIENT): Yeah. Right cheek. My sister said I look like I'm storing nuts for winter. Rude, but I do look lopsided.
[SEG0009] person_2 (CAREGIVER): It's bigger than it was yesterday. You can see it from across the room.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever with it?
[SEG0011] person_1 (PATIENT): Last night I went hot. Not terrible, just warm and achy. I meant to grab a cold cloth and then the dog was scratching and I...
[SEG0012] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Thermometer this morning said 100.2. Before we left the house.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me get a fresh set. Temperature is 100.4, pulse 96, blood pressure 136 over 84, oxygen 98 percent. So a mild fever.
[SEG0014] person_1 (PATIENT): 100.4. My cousin got to 103 with the flu and she was down a whole week, totally...
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Different situation. Any cough, or any trouble breathing?
[SEG0016] person_1 (PATIENT): No. I dumped too much pepper in the soup and my nose ran, but that's not a cough. Breathing's fine.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): And your weight, or appetite, any real change there?
[SEG0018] person_1 (PATIENT): Umm. The scale at the gym always hated me so I quit that place in March, which is not your question, sorry, I just...
[SEG0019] person_1 (PATIENT): I don't know on the weight. Soup only, cause I can't chew, so maybe less food, but I haven't been on a scale, so I can't say I actually lost any.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. We'll leave the weight. Open up, let me look.
[SEG0021] person_1 (PATIENT): Ah. Go easy.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right cheek is swollen and tender to touch. Gum around that crown is red and puffy. I don't see any pus. Jaw opens okay. Throat isn't swollen.
[SEG0023] person_1 (PATIENT): Swallowing soup is fine. Chewing is what kills me, even soft bread.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): What are you taking for it?
[SEG0025] person_1 (PATIENT): Ibuprofen. The 600 milligram tablets, every six hours, since the throbbing started. I take them with the soup so my stomach doesn't flip.
[SEG0026] person_2 (CAREGIVER): I gave her one Tylenol last night, 500 milligrams, because she felt hot. She doesn't use that regular.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Daily medicines besides that?

[SEG0028] person_1 (PATIENT): Lisinopril, 10 milligrams every morning, for my blood pressure. Been years. Oh, and last year, whenever they did bloodwork, they said my sugar was borderline. Not diabetes, they said borderline. No pill for it. I was supposed to drop soda. I mostly did, except root beer with pizza on Sundays when my brother...
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Borderline sugar, no number I can chart, and no diabetes medicine. Any allergies? Penicillin or other drugs?
[SEG0030] person_1 (PATIENT): No. Nothing. I've had penicillin, it was fine. I started to say hay fever but that's my brother, not me.
[SEG0031] person_2 (CAREGIVER): No medicine allergies. I do her pill box, I'd know.

[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thinking it through, the throb, the cheek, the low fever, right after a crown, I read that as infection under the crown, bacteria getting into the tissue so the face swells. It might only be irritation from the drilling, I can't prove a pocket of pus without the dentist's film, but I don't want to sit on it while their office is closed.
[SEG0033] person_1 (PATIENT): An infection. Great. I read people lose the tooth. My uncle lost three, but he never brushed, lived on coffee and...
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nobody's pulling a tooth today. I'm prescribing amoxicillin, 500 milligrams, by mouth, three times a day, for seven days.
[SEG0035] person_1 (PATIENT): Amoxacillin. Okay. Three a day. Does that mess with the lisinopril? And coffee, I do three cups, I almost said two, but it's three. Problem?

[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): No interaction with lisinopril that concerns me. Coffee is fine if heat doesn't set the tooth off. Keep the ibuprofen, 600 milligrams every six hours as you need it, with food. Finish every antibiotic pill even if you feel better.
[SEG0037] person_2 (CAREGIVER): 500, three times a day, seven days. I'll stick it on the fridge.

[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): If swallowing gets difficult, or breathing gets difficult, or the swelling climbs toward your eye or down into your neck, that's the emergency room. Don't wait on me or the dentist.
[SEG0039] person_1 (PATIENT): Swallowing or breathing. Okay. Right now I can...

[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right now your throat looks clear. I mean if it changes. Soft foods. Call the dentist the minute a person answers. And I want to see you back here in three days to check that cheek.
[SEG0041] person_1 (PATIENT): Three days. Their recording said something about Tuesday and then it just died, so I don't know when they're even...
[SEG0042] person_2 (CAREGIVER): I'll keep calling. I'm staying over tonight so she's not alone.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): If they can see you sooner, take it, and still keep this visit unless we cancel. Front desk will send the amoxicillin to your pharmacy.
[SEG0044] person_1 (PATIENT): Alright. Thanks. Sorry about the parking thing. And my uncle.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): You're good. Hope that cheek settles.

clinical_actions.description: Prescribe amoxicillin 500 mg by mouth three times a day for 7 days
No concerning interaction between amoxicillin and lisinopril; coffee is fine if heat does not aggravate the tooth
Continue ibuprofen 600 mg every 6 hours as needed with food
Finish the full antibiotic course even if symptoms improve
Go to the emergency room if swallowing or breathing becomes difficult or if swelling spreads to the eye or neck
Eat soft foods and call the dentist as soon as someone answers
See the dentist sooner if an opening is available and keep the clinic visit unless cancelled
Follow-up consultation
Send amoxicillin prescription to the pharmacy

spec.situation: Cheek swelling and throbbing toothache for three days after a crown; fever mild; dentist unavailable; doctor prescribes antibiotic, warns about swallowing or breathing difficulty.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

features: test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

bad.reason: Severe pain, 3 days, lower right after crown, worse chewing supported; 'certainty=certain' and current implied. 'Severity=severe' is implied, not explicit.
bad.text: Throbbing toothache (category=other, status=present, severity=severe, duration=3 days, onset=after dental crown, temporality=current, body_site=lower right tooth, aggravating_factors=chewing, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Caregiver gave one 500 mg Tylenol last night for feeling hot; not clearly 'currently_used' regularly.
bad.text: acetaminophen (dose=500 mg, frequency=once last night, indication=fever, status=currently_used, reported_by=caregiver)

bad.reason: Only prior bloodwork was mentioned; no specific completed blood sugar test documented here.

omissions.text: Patient denied any medication allergies specifically including penicillin tolerance: 'No. Nothing. I've had penicillin, it was fine.' The recorded negative finding only says 'Allergies absent' without the specific drug denial relevant to prescribing amoxicillin.
Patient reported chewing is what worsens the tooth pain and she can only tolerate soup/soft foods because she cannot chew; swallowing soup is fine.
No dysphagia currently was asked/answered indirectly: patient stated 'Swallowing soup is fine.'
Caregiver reported the right cheek swelling was worse than yesterday ('bigger than it was yesterday').
Patient had a measured temperature at home of 100.2 this morning before leaving the house.
Ibuprofen instruction included 'as needed' and to take it with food; current use also noted taken with soup so stomach doesn't get upset.
Doctor stated there was no concerning interaction between amoxicillin and lisinopril.
Patient history included borderline high blood sugar on prior bloodwork, not diabetes, with no diabetes medication.
